reflections.title: "The LORD Is with You"

reflect.text: When the angel met Gideon, Gideon was doing ordinary work and feeling overwhelmed. God greeted him as a mighty man of valor, even though Gideon was full of fear and doubt. The Lord did not give him this title because Gideon had great courage of his own. God gave it because of who God is. He meets us right in our daily tasks, regardless of our past failures or how small we feel, and views us as warriors of faith.

Feeling inadequate does not disqualify us from serving God. Gideon felt unfit, but he remained teachable and listened to the Lord. Instead of scolding him for his doubts, God patiently accommodated his weakness and built up his faith. Jesus is our ultimate man of valor who welcomes fearful people and transforms them by His grace. When we experience how patient God is with our frailty, we also learn to show that same gentle patience to the people around us.

questions: When do you feel most unqualified to do what God asks of you?
How can remembering God's gentle patience help you treat others with more grace?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank You for meeting us in our everyday routines and loving us despite our doubts. Remind us that our strength comes from who You are, not from ourselves. Help us listen to Your voice and show Your gentle patience to others today. Amen.

reflections.title: "Go in This Thy Might"

reflect.text: When the Lord told Gideon to go, He looked straight at him. That look had the power to lift Gideon out of his fear and give him courage. As F. B. Meyer observed, it was a look of expectation that stirred a timid man with fresh hope. It was also full of encouragement, assuring Gideon that the Lord would remain with him in every need. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "The Lord had looked might into him."

Gideon was naturally weak and belonged to a poor family, yet God often chooses the weak things of the world to do His work. The command to go left no room for Gideon to hesitate or waste his time. The Lord's question, "Have not I sent thee?", guarantees that God supplies the power for the task. When Christ looks upon us and sends us into our daily battles, His look imparts the strength we need to obey.

questions: What task is God calling you to step into today without hesitating?
How does knowing that the Lord sends you give you courage when you feel weak?
reflections.prayer: Lord, look upon us today and strengthen us for every duty we face. Help us not to delay or rely on our own power, but to trust that You send us. Give us holy courage as we walk in the strength You provide. Amen.

reflections.title: Called from Fear into God's Purpose

reflect.text: Gideon was threshing wheat inside a winepress, hiding in fear and humiliation from Israel's enemies. When suffering and hardship surround us, it is easy to wonder where God's wonders have gone, just as Gideon asked why the Lord seemed to have forsaken them. Gideon saw only his weakness, viewing himself as the least person in the poorest family. His low view of himself did not match what God declared about him.

We often make lists of our own flaws and limitations to argue that we cannot do what God asks. Yet when Gideon questioned God and voiced his honest confusion, the Lord did not scold him. Instead, God gave him a mission. The Lord specializes in choosing fearful, ill-equipped people so that His own power is clearly displayed. When we surrender our feelings of inadequacy to Him, God invites us to step out, seeing who we can become in His strength.

questions: What doubts about your difficult circumstances do you need to bring honestly to God?
What personal weaknesses do you need to surrender so that God can work through you?
reflections.prayer: Father, You know our fears and how often we feel too weak for the work You give us. Thank You for listening to our honest questions and for not turning away from our struggles. Take our limitations and use our lives to show Your great power. Amen.

D5.author: Jennifer Waddle
D5.work: Gideon: A Fearful Man with a Mighty Mission
